title: otel/ adapter sends landings, worker runs, suite runs and query-log deliveries as OTLP spans
goal: otel/kbmon_otel.py sends each span of kbmon --events to /v1/traces with its start and end time, a landing as one trace whose steps are child spans of the landing's span and each worker run, suite run and query-log delivery as a span with an error status when it failed

clauses.clause: otel/kbmon_otel.py sends each span of kbmon --events to /v1/traces with its start and end time, a landing as one trace whose steps are child spans of the landing's span and each worker run, suite run and query-log delivery as a span with an error status when it failed

gates.question: How is a landing's trace built?
options: one root span per land run from its first land.step to its land.end, a child span per step
one span per land.step with no root
gates.recommendation: one root span per land run from its first land.step to its land.end, a child span per step
gates.answer: one root span per land run from its first land.step to its land.end, a child span per step

ask: How does a Python span take explicit start and end times and a parent from another span?

notes: Plan 2026-10-18 (operator interview): spans for landings, worker runs, suite runs and query-log deliveries. The check decodes /v1/traces with the opentelemetry-proto package the exporter pins, run through uv. check 0 plants a random item id per run and reads only that landing's trace: ops rows come from the spool and the committed query log, which holds real landings and a stray ST-dddddddd landing from 2026-10-18
